claims.text: POL-NS-23 imposes a two-limb contact obligation before a driver may cancel for no-show: the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The platform's own trip record shows message_count 2 but in_app_calls as an empty array and call_count 0, and the derived contact_before_cancel block records obligation_met = false, with cancellation at 19:54:00 after the two messages at 19:48:00 and 19:51:30. The call limb therefore fails on the authoritative telemetry, and the fee must be voided: FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD charged, with no driver compensation.

The message limb cannot carry the obligation on its own. The chat log for this trip contains exactly two entries, both plain IN_APP text messages from the driver ('Reached Blk 106, at the drop off' at 19:48:00 and 'Waiting ah, pls come' at 19:51:30), and no voice-call entry of any kind. POL-NS-23 is conjunctive - it requires a message AND a call - so two messages with zero calls does not meet it, and the fee is voided.

The driver's counter-statement asserts 'I called her two times and messaged'. That assertion is not borne out by any artifact: the platform call ledger in the trip record is empty and the chat log carries no voice-call entry, only the two text messages quoted. The only record of a call anywhere in this case is the driver's own uncorroborated sentence, and POL-NS-23 is written against what the trip record and chat log show, not against what a party says after the fact. The rider's account - 'I never got any call from the driver, only two messages' - is the account the platform data matches, and it is the rider's account that is corroborated.

There is no open question here of the kind POL-GEN-26 exists for. Whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling is the fact POL-NS-23 turns on, and it is established by two artifacts of uncontested weight: the trip record and the chat log, each graded COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0. The one missing artifact, EV-ADVIS-06053-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, status MISSING, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), carries no fact at all and concerns road-traffic conditions, which no clause in the no-show category uses; its absence cannot unsettle a contact-obligation finding, and no outcome should be withheld on account of it.

The rider does not contest that the driver reached the pickup point: the GPS arrival check is corroborated, the nearest fix sits 1.27 m from the pickup at 4 m reported accuracy, and the driver's fix then holds at 0 kph through the wait window. That concession does not help the driver. POL-NS-21's free wait and POL-NS-23's contact obligation are separate requirements, and a punctual arrival does not cure a failure to place the required in-app call; the fee still falls.

On the money: the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.0 and refund_if_voided_sgd 5.00, so the rider is presently carrying the whole disputed charge. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION would leave that present state standing and the rider out of pocket; FULL_REFUND is the outcome the rider's claim supports, and the amount to move is the full 5.00 SGD, which matches the policy fee of 5.00 SGD so no fee-amount adjustment is in play.

This is a case the AI can finish. The amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; there is no safety flag on the dispute; and the driver's profile carries fraud_flags 0, so the 0.95 uplift is not engaged. POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final in these circumstances, so a monetary ruling - FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD fee - should issue rather than any escalation.
